consensus_summary: The fool is morally and spiritually rebellious: one who rejects God’s wisdom and lives in disobedience or practical godlessness, rather than a person of low intelligence.
book_summary: The fool is one who hears God’s word but refuses to obey it—the lawless rather than the unintelligent—and is the opposite of the wise.
consensus_core_identification: A morally and spiritually disobedient person who rejects God and divine wisdom, not an intellectually deficient person.
book_core_identification: A morally lawless person who refuses to obey God’s word, not an intellectually deficient person.
boundary_disagreement: No material boundary disagreement is evident. The book expresses the shared moral-spiritual category through the specific Matthew 7 pattern of hearing without doing. Although its wording could be read narrowly as requiring prior hearing, the consensus itself includes this pattern and treats it as a representative form of rebellion against divine wisdom.
material_contradiction: None. Both identify folly with moral and religious disobedience rather than deficient intelligence.
rationale: Reduced to their minimum cores, both readings identify the fool as the disobedient or godless person who rejects divine wisdom. The book’s terms “will not do it” and “lawless” specify the same practical rebellion described by the consensus. Calling the wise the opposite also agrees with the wisdom-literature framework represented in the responses.
strongest_objection: The phrase “one who hears God’s word” might narrow the category to people who have received explicit instruction and knowingly refuse it, whereas the consensus also includes broader practical godlessness, arrogance, or imprudence. In context, however, this is best read as a concrete formulation of the same core rather than a deliberate exclusion of those cases.
